data.narrative:
Type One Energy is a Series B nuclear energy company founded by David Anderson, Chris Hegna, and John Canik that has raised $100M+. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 11 peers across nuclear energy—three public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private firms including Valar Atomics, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and Fuse Energy.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method. Using the $100M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B to later-stage progression, this approach yields $190M. A peer-median triangulation was not viable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage nuclear peers with comparable valuation data—only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage datapoint were identified, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum threshold for statistical reliability.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M to $218M, with a median point of $190M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method and highlights the key uncertainty: the scarcity of comparable-stage, nuclear-focused private companies limits cross-validation. Stage-progression methodology assumes Type One follows standard venture cadence, which may not hold in frontier energy sectors where development cycles and capital requirements diverge materially from software or traditional cleantech benchmarks. Additional data on nuclear peer financing outcomes or later rounds would strengthen conviction in this range.
